details:
**Mr. Collins and Charlotte Lucas**
Mr. William Collins is a pompous, obsequious clergyman and Mr. Bennet's cousin. Because the estate of Longbourn is entailed to male heirs, he will inherit it. He first proposes to Elizabeth Bennet, who refuses him. Within days he becomes engaged to her practical friend Charlotte Lucas, who marries him for security.

**Lydia's elopement with George Wickham**
Lydia, the youngest and most flirtatious Bennet sister, runs off with the charming but dishonest militia officer George Wickham while visiting Brighton. The scandal threatens the whole family's reputation. Mr. Darcy secretly tracks the couple down, pays Wickham's debts, and bribes him into marrying her. Wickham grew up alongside Darcy as the son of the elder Mr. Darcy's steward.

**Lady Catherine de Bourgh**
Lady Catherine is Mr. Darcy's domineering, snobbish aunt. She lives at the estate of Rosings in Kent and is Mr. Collins's patron, whom he flatters endlessly. Late in the novel she visits Longbourn and demands that Elizabeth promise never to accept Darcy. Elizabeth refuses to make that promise.

**"It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife."**
This is the famous ironic opening sentence of the novel, published in 1813. It introduces the arrival of the wealthy Mr. Bingley and the marriage-obsessed world of the Bennet family, especially Mrs. Bennet.

**Charles Bingley, Jane Bennet, and Netherfield Park**
The novel begins when the wealthy, good-natured Charles Bingley rents Netherfield Park, near the village of Meryton and the Bennets' home at Longbourn. He falls for Jane, the eldest and gentlest Bennet sister. They are separated for a time, but he eventually proposes and marries her.

**"Tolerable, but not handsome enough to tempt me"**
At the opening assembly ball in Meryton, Elizabeth overhears Darcy say this about her. Just before, he had told Bingley that Bingley was "dancing with the only handsome girl in the room," meaning Jane. The insult forms Elizabeth's poor first impression of Darcy, the "prejudice" of the title.

**Pemberley and Mrs. Reynolds**
Pemberley is Darcy's grand estate in Derbyshire. Elizabeth tours it with her aunt and uncle, the Gardiners. There the housekeeper, Mrs. Reynolds, praises Darcy's kindness and shows them a portrait of him, which helps change Elizabeth's opinion of him. Elizabeth later jokes that her love for him dates from first seeing Pemberley's grounds.

**Jane's ride in the rain and Elizabeth's muddy walk**
Mrs. Bennet sends Jane to Netherfield on horseback rather than by carriage, hoping rain will force her to stay overnight near Bingley. Jane catches a fever and is stuck there. Elizabeth then walks about three miles across muddy fields to nurse her. The Bingley sisters sneer that her petticoat is "six inches deep in mud."

**The Gardiners**
Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner are Mrs. Bennet's brother and his wife. They are sensible, kind relatives who live in London, and Jane stays with them for a time. They take Elizabeth on the tour of Derbyshire where she visits Pemberley. Mrs. Gardiner earlier warns Elizabeth against getting involved with Wickham.

**Georgiana Darcy and Mrs. Younge**
Georgiana is Darcy's shy younger sister, who is skilled at the piano. Before the novel begins, Wickham tried to elope with her to get her fortune, helped by her companion Mrs. Younge. Darcy reveals this history to Elizabeth in his letter. Caroline Bingley flatters Georgiana in hopes of winning Darcy.

**Darcy's first proposal, "In vain I have struggled. It will not do."**
Darcy's first proposal to Elizabeth at Hunsford in Kent begins with these words, but he insults her family while proposing, and she angrily rejects him. He then gives her a letter explaining his conduct toward Wickham and why he separated Bingley from Jane. After reading it, Elizabeth realizes her own prejudice and exclaims, "Till this moment I never knew myself."

**Caroline Bingley**
Caroline is Bingley's snobbish sister, who lives with him at Netherfield along with her sister Louisa Hurst. She wants Darcy for herself. She mocks Darcy for admiring Elizabeth's "fine eyes," belittles Elizabeth's looks (including calling her teeth merely "tolerable"), and helps persuade Bingley to leave Jane.

**Fordyce's Sermons**
Mr. Collins reads aloud to the Bennet girls from this book of sermons on female conduct. Lydia interrupts him with gossip about the militia officers, offending him. He gives up and plays backgammon with Mr. Bennet instead.

**Mary Bennet's singing at the Netherfield ball**
Mary is the bookish, pedantic middle Bennet sister. At the Netherfield ball she insists on singing and playing the piano despite her weak voice, which mortifies Elizabeth. Her performance is one of several embarrassing family displays that evening.

**"From this day you must be a stranger to one of your parents"**
Mr. Bennet says this dryly to Elizabeth after she refuses Mr. Collins. He explains that her mother will never see her again if she does not marry Collins, and he will never see her again if she does.
